items.quote: The San Diego Zoo is a zoo in San Diego, California, United States, located in Balboa Park
items.note: Balboa Park article confirms the 1915 Panama-California Exposition.

items.quote: It commemorates the landing of Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo at San Diego Bay on September 28, 1542
items.note: His nationality (Portuguese or Spanish) is disputed, which does not affect this question. Accept 'Cabrillo'.

items.quote: it was founded on July 16, 1769, by Spanish friar Junípero Serra
items.note: Answer is right, but the 'first' clue is looser than it looks: Wikipedia calls it 'the second Franciscan-founded mission in the Californias (after San Fernando de Velicata)', which Serra also founded, in Baja California. It is the first of the 21 Alta California missions. Optional tightening: 'the first of the 21 missions in what is now the US state of California'.

items.quote: The USS Midway was the United States' longest-serving aircraft carrier of the 20th century, from 1945 to 1992
items.note: Decommissioned 11 April 1992; museum on Navy Pier since 2004.

items.quote: The San Diego Padres are an American professional baseball team based in San Diego
items.note: An easy one; fine as a warm-up.

items.quote: Founded in 1970, originally showcasing primarily comic books and science fiction/fantasy media, Comic-Con has grown to include a large range of pop culture and entertainment elements across virtually all genres
items.note: Not at risk of relocating soon: the article notes an announcement that it is staying in San Diego through 2030.

items.quote: is a prestressed concrete/steel girder fixed-link bridge crossing over San Diego Bay, linking San Diego with Coronado, California
items.note: Opened to traffic 3 August 1969 (same article). Technically Coronado is on a peninsula, but it is an incorporated city, so 'neighboring city' is accurate.
